input.question: Why are some many comets peanut-shaped?
input.ground_truth: That's what you get if two roughly spherical solid objects approach each other slowly and stick together. [Ultima Thule](_URL_1_) is a good example, you can clearly see the two components. For asteroids near Earth we have enough data for statistics: [10-15% are contact binaries](_URL_0_).

Question: Why are some many comets peanut-shaped?

Okay! Imagine a comet is like a big, dirty snowball that flies around the sun. Now, when this snowball gets close to the sun, the sun’s heat makes some of the ice on the comet turn into gas. This gas pushes out from the middle of the comet and makes the two ends get stretched out. 

But the middle of the comet is stronger, so it doesn’t stretch as much as the sides. That’s why, when you look at it from far away, the comet looks like a peanut! It’s kind of like if you squish a marshmallow between your hands and it gets longer in the middle but keeps its round ends. That’s why some comets look like peanuts!
